title: The Conquest of Ireland: How England Never Left (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听 Leonardo English 的 English Learning for Curious Minds。在这个节目里，你可以一边听引人入胜的故事，了解世界上各种奇妙的事物，一边提高英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today it's the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on the nine centuries of struggle between Ireland and England.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge。今天我们要开始一个新的三集系列节目，这次的主题是爱尔兰与英格兰之间长达九个世纪的斗争。

sentences.en: In today's episode, we go back to the very beginning: the moment when the first English-backed soldiers stepped ashore in Ireland — and how what began as a temporary military favour became, over the following five centuries, a permanent and deeply painful occupation.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将回到最初的起点：第一批由英国支持的士兵在爱尔兰登陆的那一刻——以及最初的一场临时军事援助，是如何在接下来的五个世纪里演变成一场持久且极其痛苦的占领的。

sentences.en: In part two, we move to the nineteenth century: the Act of Union, the catastrophic Great Famine, and how the relationship broke down, seemingly, beyond repair.
sentences.zh: 在第二部分，我们将转向 19 世纪：包括《联合法案》、灾难性的“大饥荒”，以及两国关系如何陷入看似无法修复的破裂。

sentences.en: And in part three, we will follow Ireland through rebellion to independence.
sentences.zh: 在第三部分，我们将追随爱尔兰从反抗走向独立的历程。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，事不宜迟，让我们直接进入正题。

sentences.en: Now, before we go anywhere, let me paint a picture of where today's episode — and this entire mini-series — will be taking place.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前，让我先为大家描绘一下今天这集节目——以及整个系列节目——所发生的地理背景。

sentences.en: The British Isles, as they are sometimes called, are the group of islands off the north-west coast of Europe.
sentences.zh: 不列颠群岛（British Isles），有时人们这样称呼它们，是位于欧洲西北海岸的一组群岛。

sentences.en: The largest island is Britain, which is made up of three countries: England in the south and east, Scotland in the north, and Wales to the west.
sentences.zh: 最大的岛屿是不列颠岛（Britain），由三个国家组成：南边和东边的英格兰（England）、北边的苏格兰（Scotland）以及西边的威尔士（Wales）。

sentences.en: Each of those countries also includes some smaller islands, and there is the added complication of some islands that are something confusing called crown dependencies, but that's too much detail for today.
sentences.zh: 这些国家还各自包含一些较小的岛屿，此外还有一些被称为“王权属地”（crown dependencies）的岛屿，情况比较复杂，但今天就不细说了。

sentences.en: Just to the west of Britain, across a stretch of water called the Irish Sea, lies an island called Ireland.
sentences.zh: 就在不列颠岛的西边，隔着一片被称为爱尔兰海（Irish Sea）的海域，坐落着一个叫爱尔兰（Ireland）的岛屿。

sentences.en: It's a smaller island than Britain. It's roughly the size of Portugal.
sentences.zh: 它比不列颠岛小，面积大约和葡萄牙相当。

sentences.en: It's green, rainy, and incredibly beautiful.
sentences.zh: 那里绿草如茵，多雨，而且美得令人惊叹。

sentences.en: And today, if you look at a map of Ireland, you will notice something unusual.
sentences.zh: 如今，如果你看一眼爱尔兰地图，你会发现一些不寻常的地方。

sentences.en: The island is divided into two parts. The larger part — twenty-six counties in the south, west, and centre — forms the Republic of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 这个岛被分成了两部分。较大的部分——位于南部、西部和中部的 26 个郡——组成了爱尔兰共和国（Republic of Ireland）。

sentences.en: It is an independent country and a full member of the European Union.
sentences.zh: 它是一个独立国家，也是欧盟的正式成员国。

sentences.en: The smaller part — the six counties in the north-east — is called Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 较小的部分——东北部的 6 个郡——被称为北爱尔兰（Northern Ireland）。

sentences.en: It is part of the United Kingdom, alongside England, Scotland, and Wales, and it's governed ultimately from London.
sentences.zh: 它是联合王国（United Kingdom）的一部分，与英格兰、苏格兰和威尔士并列，最终由伦敦政府管辖。

sentences.en: This, confusingly, makes Northern Ireland part of the geographical area of Ireland, the island of Ireland, but separate from the country of Ireland, the Republic of Ireland, to give it its full name.
sentences.zh: 这就造成了一种困惑：北爱尔兰在地理上属于爱尔兰岛，但在政治上却独立于爱尔兰这个国家（全称爱尔兰共和国）。

sentences.en: This division is not some ancient accident of geography.
sentences.zh: 这种划分并非某种古老的地理偶然。

sentences.en: It is the direct result of decisions made just over a hundred years ago.
sentences.zh: 它是 100 多年前所做决定的直接结果。

sentences.en: And those decisions were themselves the product of a relationship between Ireland and England — and later Ireland and Britain — a relationship that goes back nine hundred years.
sentences.zh: 而这些决定本身又是爱尔兰与英格兰（后来是爱尔兰与英国）之间关系的产物，这种关系可以追溯到 900 年前。

sentences.en: This is what this mini-series is about: not the complete history of Ireland, but a journey through the key events that shaped the Ireland we know today.
sentences.zh: 这就是本系列节目的主题：不是完整的爱尔兰历史，而是通过关键事件带大家了解爱尔兰是如何变成今天这个样子的。

sentences.en: And one more thing before we begin, let me quickly introduce the main characters — or rather, the main groups — because it can get confusing quickly.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前还有一件事，让我快速介绍一下主要角色——或者说是主要群体——因为情况很快就会变得复杂。

sentences.en: In the twelfth century, when our story begins, Ireland was home to the Gaelic Irish — a Celtic people with their own language, their own laws, and their own system of kingship.
sentences.zh: 在 12 世纪，也就是我们的故事开始时，爱尔兰是盖尔爱尔兰人（Gaelic Irish）的家园——他们是凯尔特民族，拥有自己的语言、法律和王权制度。

sentences.en: At this point, Ireland was not a unified country.
sentences.zh: 此时的爱尔兰并不是一个统一的国家。

sentences.en: It was a patchwork of kingdoms, clans, and territories.
sentences.zh: 它是由许多王国、氏族和领地拼凑而成的。

sentences.en: There was the High King sitting loosely at the top, but his authority was limited and often more symbolic than absolute.
sentences.zh: 虽然名义上有一位“至尊王”（High King）居于顶端，但他的权力有限，往往象征意义大于实际统治力。

sentences.en: Irish politics was fluid, competitive, and often violent.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰的政治局势多变、充满竞争，且往往伴随着暴力。

sentences.en: Kings rose and fell. Alliances shifted. To the east, by the twelfth century, England had already gone through one major change of power.
sentences.zh: 国王兴衰更替，盟友不断变换。到了 12 世纪，东边的英格兰已经经历了一次重大的政权更迭。

sentences.en: In 1066, a group from Normandy in northern France had invaded England under William the Conqueror and taken over the country.
sentences.zh: 1066 年，一群来自法国北部诺曼底的人在“征服者威廉”（William the Conqueror）的率领下入侵并占领了英格兰。

sentences.en: These were the Normans. These Normans were exceptional soldiers.
sentences.zh: 他们就是诺曼人（Normans）。这些诺曼人是极其出色的士兵。

sentences.en: They spoke Norman-French. They were Catholic.
sentences.zh: 他们说诺曼法语，信奉天主教。

sentences.en: And they brought with them a feudal system of land ownership quite different from anything in the Gaelic world, a system in which land was controlled through a hierarchy of lords and tenants.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了一套与盖尔世界完全不同的封建土地所有制，在这种制度下，土地通过领主和租户的等级制度进行控制。

sentences.en: So when people talk about "the English" arriving in Ireland, what they really mean — at first, at least — is Anglo-Normans.
sentences.zh: 所以，当人们谈论“英国人”到达爱尔兰时，他们真正的意思——至少最初是这样——是指盎格鲁-诺曼人（Anglo-Normans）。

sentences.en: The ruling class of England was Norman. The soldiers who would cross the Irish Sea were Norman.
sentences.zh: 当时英格兰的统治阶级是诺曼人，跨越爱尔兰海的士兵也是诺曼人。

sentences.en: The language they brought was Norman-French.
sentences.zh: 他们带来的语言是诺曼法语。

sentences.en: The name "English" came later. Right. Now let us begin.
sentences.zh: “英国人”这个称呼是后来才有的。好了，现在让我们开始吧。

sentences.en: In 1166, a king was on the run. His name was Diarmait Mac Murchada and he was the King of Leinster.
sentences.zh: 1166 年，一位国王正在逃亡。他的名字叫 Diarmait Mac Murchada，是伦斯特（Leinster）的国王。

sentences.en: Leinster is the eastern province of Ireland, the area that includes what is now Dublin.
sentences.zh: 伦斯特是爱尔兰东部的省份，包括现在的都柏林地区。

sentences.en: He had been expelled by the High King of Ireland, with the backing of a rival chieftain named Tigernán Ua Ruairc — a man with a very personal reason to want Diarmait gone.
sentences.zh: 他被爱尔兰至尊王驱逐了，背后支持者是一位名叫 Tigernán Ua Ruairc 的敌对酋长——此人有一个非常私人的理由想要赶走 Diarmait。

sentences.en: Years earlier, Diarmait had abducted Tigernán's wife.
sentences.zh: 几年前，Diarmait 绑架了 Tigernán 的妻子。

sentences.en: And back then, like today, this wasn't something that most people took kindly to, and the grudge had never faded.
sentences.zh: 无论在当时还是现在，这种事大多数人都无法容忍，而且这份积怨从未消散。

sentences.en: When he was expelled, Diarmait did what many rulers in trouble do: he went looking for allies.
sentences.zh: 被驱逐后，Diarmait 做了许多陷入困境的统治者都会做的事：寻找盟友。

sentences.en: He crossed to Britain, then to northern France, where he found King Henry II of England.
sentences.zh: 他前往不列颠，然后去了法国北部，在那里找到了英格兰国王 Henry II。

sentences.en: He asked Henry for permission to recruit soldiers from among his lords.
sentences.zh: 他请求 Henry 允许他从其领主中招募士兵。

sentences.en: Now, Henry had no interest in invading Ireland himself.
sentences.zh: 当时，Henry 本人对入侵爱尔兰并无兴趣。

sentences.en: He had territories stretching from Scotland to southern France, and keeping them together was already a full-time occupation.
sentences.zh: 他的领土从苏格兰延伸到法国南部，维持这些领土的统一已经让他分身乏术了。

sentences.en: But he gave Diarmait a letter, essentially a royal permission slip, saying that if any of his English lords wanted to help this exiled Irish king, they were free to do so.
sentences.zh: 但他给了 Diarmait 一封信，基本上是一张皇家许可条，声明如果他的任何英国领主想帮助这位流亡的爱尔兰国王，他们可以自由行动。

sentences.en: The lord who took up this offer was a man named Richard de Clare, the Earl of Pembroke.
sentences.zh: 接受这一提议的领主是一位名叫 Richard de Clare 的人，即彭布罗克伯爵。

sentences.en: History remembers him by his nickname: Strongbow.
sentences.zh: 历史记住了他的绰号：Strongbow（强弓）。

sentences.en: And if you have spent much time in British pubs, you might remember this name as a type of not-exactly-delicious cider.
sentences.zh: 如果你在英国酒吧待过很长时间，你可能会记得这个名字，它是一种味道并不怎么样的苹果酒品牌。

sentences.en: Now, Strongbow was not doing this out of the kindness of his heart.
sentences.zh: Strongbow 这样做并不是出于好心。

sentences.en: It was a business arrangement. Strongbow would provide soldiers and military skill.
sentences.zh: 这是一场商业交易。Strongbow 提供士兵和军事技能。

sentences.en: In return, he would get Diarmait's daughter Aoife in marriage, and the right to inherit the Kingdom of Leinster when Diarmait died.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，他将迎娶 Diarmait 的女儿 Aoife，并有权在 Diarmait 去世后继承伦斯特王国。

sentences.en: Strongbow landed in the south of Ireland in 1170 with around a thousand men.
sentences.zh: 1170 年，Strongbow 率领约一千人登陆爱尔兰南部。

sentences.en: Within months, his men had helped capture the cities of Waterford and Dublin.
sentences.zh: 几个月内，他的部下就协助攻占了沃特福德和都柏林。

sentences.en: A year later, Diarmait was dead, and Strongbow was King of Leinster.
sentences.zh: 一年后，Diarmait 去世，Strongbow 成为了伦斯特国王。

sentences.en: Shortly afterwards, Henry II arrived, and not to congratulate him.
sentences.zh: 随后不久，Henry II 到了，但他不是来祝贺的。

sentences.en: Henry was alarmed. A powerful Norman lord establishing a semi-independent kingdom in Ireland, outside his control, was the last thing he had intended.
sentences.zh: Henry 感到警觉。一个强大的诺曼领主在爱尔兰建立一个脱离他控制的半独立王国，这绝不是他的本意。

sentences.en: He arrived with a large fleet — reportedly around four hundred ships — and marched into Waterford.
sentences.zh: 他带着一支庞大的舰队抵达——据报道约有 400 艘船——并进入了沃特福德。

sentences.en: Strongbow submitted to him, and so too did a number of Irish kings.
sentences.zh: Strongbow 向他臣服，许多爱尔兰国王也纷纷效仿。

sentences.en: Now, why did the Irish kings submit so readily?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么爱尔兰国王们如此轻易就臣服了呢？

sentences.en: Well, a few reasons. Firstly, Henry was the most powerful king in Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 原因有几个。首先，Henry 是西欧最强大的国王。

sentences.en: His army was far larger than anything Ireland could field.
sentences.zh: 他的军队规模远超爱尔兰所能集结的任何力量。

sentences.en: But there was something else at work too.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一个因素在起作用。

sentences.en: Many Irish kings were more worried about Strongbow than about Henry.
sentences.zh: 许多爱尔兰国王对 Strongbow 的担忧超过了对 Henry 的担忧。

sentences.en: A Norman lord controlling Leinster and Dublin was a direct, immediate threat to their own territories.
sentences.zh: 一个控制着伦斯特和都柏林的诺曼领主，对他们自己的领地构成了直接且迫在眉睫的威胁。

sentences.en: Henry, by contrast, was far away and apparently had no wish to rule Ireland directly.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，Henry 远在天边，而且显然没有直接统治爱尔兰的愿望。

sentences.en: It seemed like a smarter plan to give a distant king a title on paper than to fight the Normans on their own doorstep.
sentences.zh: 与其在自家门口与诺曼人开战，给远方的国王一个名义上的头衔似乎是更明智的选择。

sentences.en: So they submitted. In practice, this looked like it meant very little, at first at least.
sentences.zh: 于是他们臣服了。在实践中，这在最初看起来似乎没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: Henry was not dismantling Irish kingdoms.
sentences.zh: Henry 并没有废除爱尔兰的王国。

sentences.en: He was not replacing Irish kings with English governors.
sentences.zh: 他也没有用英国总督取代爱尔兰国王。

sentences.en: He was simply asking them to acknowledge him as their overlord — to place him at the top of the chain of loyalty, while leaving Irish kings free to rule their own territories as before.
sentences.zh: 他只是要求他们承认他为宗主——将他置于忠诚链的最顶端，同时让爱尔兰国王们像以前一样自由地统治自己的领地。

sentences.en: It was, in other words, a relatively light touch.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是一种相对温和的干预。

sentences.en: Henry took pledges of loyalty, brought Strongbow firmly under his authority, and sailed home the following year.
sentences.zh: Henry 接受了忠诚宣誓，将 Strongbow 牢牢置于自己的权威之下，并于次年启程回国。

sentences.en: For most of Ireland, life went on exactly as before.
sentences.zh: 对爱尔兰大部分地区来说，生活照旧。

sentences.en: But something important had happened. By 1171, the English — or more precisely, the Anglo-Normans — they had established a foothold in Ireland, and they would never entirely let go.
sentences.zh: 但重要的事情已经发生了。到 1171 年，英国人——或者更准确地说，盎格鲁-诺曼人——已经在爱尔兰站稳了脚跟，并且再也没有完全离开。

sentences.en: Now, you will forgive me if I skip forward by a couple of centuries here.
sentences.zh: 请原谅我在这里跳过几个世纪。

sentences.en: What happened between 1170 and the late 1400s is a long story — and for our purposes, the key thing to understand is this: the English presence in Ireland was real, it existed, but it was pretty limited in practice.
sentences.zh: 1170 年到 1400 年代后期发生的事情说来话长——对我们而言，关键要理解的是：英国在爱尔兰的存在是真实的，它确实存在，但在实践中相当有限。

sentences.en: The Normans introduced English law and a feudal system of land ownership quite different from the previous Gaelic model.
sentences.zh: 诺曼人引入了英国法律和封建土地所有制，这与之前的盖尔模式截然不同。

sentences.en: They built castles, established new centres of power, and reshaped many Irish towns.
sentences.zh: 他们建造城堡，建立新的权力中心，并重塑了许多爱尔兰城镇。

sentences.en: But they never controlled the whole island.
sentences.zh: 但他们从未控制过整个岛屿。

sentences.en: The area of reliable English rule, which centred on Dublin, was called the Pale.
sentences.zh: 以都柏林为中心、受英国可靠统治的地区被称为“围栏区”（the Pale）。

sentences.en: A pale, P-A-L-E, as a noun, is literally a fenced boundary, an enclosure.
sentences.zh: “Pale”这个词作为名词，字面意思是栅栏边界或围场。

sentences.en: You might know the expression to be " beyond the pale ", and this is where it comes from.
sentences.zh: 你可能知道“beyond the pale”（出格、无法接受）这个表达，它就是由此而来的。

sentences.en: Originally, to be beyond the Pale was to be outside the ordered English world — but the phrase passed into the English language to mean something unacceptable, outside the boundaries of civilised behaviour.
sentences.zh: 最初，“beyond the Pale”是指处于有序的英国世界之外——但这个短语后来进入了英语语言，意指不可接受、超出文明行为界限的事情。

sentences.en: And beyond the Pale, Gaelic Ireland continued much as before, with its own chiefs, its own laws, its own language and its own culture.
sentences.zh: 而在“围栏区”之外，盖尔爱尔兰基本上维持原样，拥有自己的首领、法律、语言和文化。

sentences.en: And then something happened that you might think was perfectly predictable, but that took the English Crown by surprise.
sentences.zh: 接着发生了一件你可能认为完全可以预见、却让英国王室措手不及的事情。

sentences.en: Many Norman families, who were living side by side with the Gaelic Irish, they gradually absorbed Irish ways.
sentences.zh: 许多与盖尔爱尔兰人并肩生活的诺曼家庭逐渐吸收了爱尔兰的生活方式。

sentences.en: They learned the Irish language. They adopted Irish customs.
sentences.zh: 他们学习爱尔兰语，采纳爱尔兰习俗。

sentences.en: They intermarried with local families. They became known as the Old English.
sentences.zh: 他们与当地家庭通婚，被称为“老英格兰人”（Old English）。

sentences.en: The settlers were becoming, it was said, "more Irish than the Irish themselves."
sentences.zh: 据说，这些定居者变得“比爱尔兰人还像爱尔兰人”。

sentences.en: The English Crown spent decades trying to stop this.
sentences.zh: 英国王室花了数十年时间试图阻止这种情况。

sentences.en: Laws were passed in the 14th century trying to ban English settlers from speaking Irish, wearing Irish clothes, or from marrying Irish people.
sentences.zh: 14 世纪通过了一些法律，试图禁止英国定居者说爱尔兰语、穿爱尔兰衣服或与爱尔兰人结婚。

sentences.en: They were largely ignored. English law in Ireland was, in other words, a paper tiger — a rule that looked powerful on paper but had no real substance when it came to enforcement.
sentences.zh: 这些法律在很大程度上被忽视了。换句话说，爱尔兰的英国法律只是一只“纸老虎”——在纸面上看起来很强大，但在执行时却毫无实质内容。

sentences.en: So by the early sixteenth century, meaningful English control had shrunk back to a narrow strip around Dublin.
sentences.zh: 因此，到 16 世纪初，英国的实质控制范围已缩减至都柏林周围的一条狭长地带。

sentences.en: The rest of the island was governed by Gaelic and Anglo-Irish lords who paid little attention to the Crown in London.
sentences.zh: 岛上的其余部分由盖尔和盎格鲁-爱尔兰领主统治，他们几乎不理会伦敦的王室。

sentences.en: All was well and good, but then Anne Boleyn arrived.
sentences.zh: 这一切本来相安无事，但接着 Anne Boleyn 出现了。

sentences.en: Or rather, Henry VIII decided he wanted to marry Anne Boleyn, this led him to break with Rome, and this had knock-on lasting consequences for Ireland.
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，Henry VIII 决定要娶 Anne Boleyn，这导致他与罗马教廷决裂，并对爱尔兰产生了连锁且深远的影响。

sentences.en: As a quick reminder, in 1534 Henry VIII officially broke with the Catholic Church in Rome and established the Church of England — a new, Protestant church under his own authority rather than the Pope's.
sentences.zh: 简单回顾一下，1534 年 Henry VIII 正式与罗马天主教会决裂，并建立了英格兰教会（Church of England）——这是一个由他自己而非教皇管辖的新新教教会。

sentences.en: He wanted Ireland to follow, but it remained stubbornly Catholic.
sentences.zh: 他希望爱尔兰也随之改变，但爱尔兰顽固地坚持信仰天主教。

sentences.en: The Irish kept their priests, their Mass, and their loyalty to Rome.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰人保留了他们的神父、弥撒以及对罗马的忠诚。

sentences.en: For the English Crown, this wasn't just a religious insult; it was a massive security risk.
sentences.zh: 对英国王室来说，这不仅是宗教上的侮辱，更是巨大的安全风险。

sentences.en: In an age of Catholic superpowers like Spain and France, a Catholic Ireland was seen as a potential " backdoor," a place where England’s enemies could land an army and launch an invasion on London’s doorstep.
sentences.zh: 在西班牙和法国等天主教超级大国并立的时代，天主教爱尔兰被视为一个潜在的“后门”，英国的敌人可以从这里登陆军队，在伦敦的家门口发动入侵。

sentences.en: So, in 1541, Henry VIII declared himself King of Ireland, an upgrade from the previous title of Lord.
sentences.zh: 于是，在 1541 年，Henry VIII 宣布自己为爱尔兰国王，这是对他之前“领主”头衔的升级。

sentences.en: This was a clear signal that he intended to rule the entire island, not just manage it from afar.
sentences.zh: 这是一个明确的信号，表明他打算统治整个岛屿，而不仅仅是远距离管理。

sentences.en: To secure this " backdoor," he launched a policy called " surrender and regrant ".
sentences.zh: 为了守住这个“后门”，他发起了一项名为“投降与重授”（surrender and regrant）的政策。

sentences.en: The idea was to bring Irish lords formally into the English legal system by making them English subjects on paper.
sentences.zh: 其核心思想是通过在名义上将爱尔兰领主变为英国臣民，从而将他们正式纳入英国法律体系。

sentences.en: Under this policy, they would give up their traditional Gaelic titles, acknowledge Henry as king, and receive their lands back as English-style grants with titles like Earl or Baron.
sentences.zh: 根据这项政策，他们将放弃传统的盖尔头衔，承认 Henry 为国王，并以伯爵或男爵等英国式头衔重新获得自己的土地。

sentences.en: Some agreed, because it seemed like a practical compromise: recognition from the Crown, while keeping their lands and local power.
sentences.zh: 有些人同意了，因为这看起来像是一种务实的妥协：既能获得王室的认可，又能保留自己的土地和地方权力。

sentences.en: Many did not. And over time, those who refused would increasingly be treated not as semi-independent rulers, but as obstacles to be subdued.
sentences.zh: 许多人并不同意。随着时间的推移，那些拒绝的人越来越不被视为半独立的统治者，而是被视为必须征服的障碍。

sentences.en: And those who did agree often found, in the following generations, that they had stumbled into a trap.
sentences.zh: 而那些同意的人往往在后代中发现，他们掉进了一个陷阱。

sentences.en: Under Gaelic tradition, land belonged to the clan — it was managed by the lord on behalf of his people, and leadership passed not necessarily to the lord's eldest son, but to whoever the clan chose.
sentences.zh: 根据盖尔传统，土地属于氏族——由领主代表其人民管理，领导权不一定传给领主的长子，而是由氏族选择。

sentences.en: Under English law, land was the lord's personal property, and passed to his eldest son.
sentences.zh: 而根据英国法律，土地是领主的个人财产，并传给其长子。

sentences.en: So when an Irish lord agreed to " surrender and regrant," he was unknowingly converting his clan 's shared land into his own private estate under English law.
sentences.zh: 因此，当一位爱尔兰领主同意“投降与重授”时，他是在不知不觉中根据英国法律将氏族的共有土地变成了他自己的私有财产。

sentences.en: The people who had always farmed that land suddenly had no legal claim to it.
sentences.zh: 那些世世代代耕种那片土地的人突然间在法律上失去了对土地的所有权。

sentences.en: Disputes over who actually owned what would simmer for generations.
sentences.zh: 关于谁到底拥有什么的争端持续了好几代人。

sentences.en: Now, Henry VIII died in 1547, leaving Ireland unsettled, only partially subdued, and deeply unconvinced by Protestantism.
sentences.zh: Henry VIII 于 1547 年去世，留下了一个动荡不安、仅被部分征服且对新教深表怀疑的爱尔兰。

sentences.en: His son Edward VI and his daughter Mary tried different approaches — Mary, who was Catholic, actually started the first plantations in the Irish midlands, confiscating land from Irish lords and giving it to English settlers.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子 Edward VI 和女儿 Mary 尝试了不同的方法——信奉天主教的 Mary 实际上在爱尔兰中部开始了第一批“植民”（plantations），没收爱尔兰领主的土地并分给英国定居者。

sentences.en: But it was Henry's other daughter who would bring the crisis to a head.
sentences.zh: 但最终是 Henry 的另一个女儿将危机推向了顶峰。

sentences.en: Elizabeth I decided that the time for half-measures was over.
sentences.zh: Elizabeth I 决定，采取折中办法的时代已经结束了。

sentences.en: Under her reign, England committed large armies to Ireland with a single goal: full military conquest of the entire island, not just the management of the Pale.
sentences.zh: 在她的统治下，英格兰向爱尔兰派出了大军，目标只有一个：对整个岛屿进行全面的军事征服，而不仅仅是管理“围栏区”。

sentences.en: This transformed the nature of the conflict entirely.
sentences.zh: 这彻底改变了冲突的性质。

sentences.en: We are no longer talking about diplomacy and land grants.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的不再是外交和土地授予。

sentences.en: We are talking about English soldiers stationed all over the country, and ultimately, war.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是驻扎在全国各地的英国士兵，以及最终的战争。

sentences.en: The most serious of these conflicts — and the one that came closest to undoing English rule in Ireland entirely — was called the Nine Years' War.
sentences.zh: 这些冲突中最严重的一次——也是最接近彻底推翻英国在爱尔兰统治的一次——被称为“九年战争”。

sentences.en: This began in 1593, and was led by a man named Hugh O'Neill, who had been educated in England, who understood English politics from the inside, and who held his title from the English Crown.
sentences.zh: 这场战争始于 1593 年，由一个名叫 Hugh O'Neill 的人领导，他曾在英格兰受过教育，从内部了解英国政治，并拥有英国王室授予的头衔。

sentences.en: An unlikely profile for someone who would become the leader of the last great Gaelic resistance to English rule.
sentences.zh: 对于一个即将成为最后一次伟大的盖尔人反抗英国统治领袖的人来说，这样的背景确实出人意料。

sentences.en: Now, O'Neill was patient, organised, and extremely effective.
sentences.zh: O'Neill 很有耐心，组织严密，且极具效率。

sentences.en: He trained his men in modern European military tactics rather than traditional Irish methods.
sentences.zh: 他用现代欧洲军事战术而非传统的爱尔兰方法训练部下。

sentences.en: And at the Battle of Yellow Ford in 1598, in the north of Ireland, his forces surrounded and destroyed an entire English army column, killing around two thousand soldiers.
sentences.zh: 在 1598 年爱尔兰北部的黄福德战役（Battle of Yellow Ford）中，他的部队包围并摧毁了整支英国军队纵队，杀死了约两千名士兵。

sentences.en: For a moment, it seemed Ireland could actually be lost, or rather, won back, for the Irish.
sentences.zh: 有那么一刻，爱尔兰似乎真的要脱离英国掌控，或者更确切地说，被爱尔兰人夺回。

sentences.en: O’Neill then sought help from Elizabeth’s great enemy, Spain, which was more than happy to assist.
sentences.zh: O'Neill 随后向 Elizabeth 的宿敌西班牙寻求帮助，西班牙非常乐意提供援助。

sentences.en: In 1601, a Spanish force landed at Kinsale, on the south coast of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 1601 年，一支西班牙军队在爱尔兰南海岸的金赛尔（Kinsale）登陆。

sentences.en: O’Neill marched his army all the way south from Ulster to join them.
sentences.zh: O'Neill 率领军队从北部的阿尔斯特（Ulster）一路南下与他们会合。

sentences.en: But this was the problem: the Spanish had landed far from O’Neill’s power base, and before the two forces could properly unite, the English moved against them.
sentences.zh: 但问题就在这里：西班牙人的登陆地点远离 O'Neill 的权力基地，在两支力量能够妥善汇合之前，英军就对他们采取了行动。

sentences.en: At the Battle of Kinsale, the Irish and Spanish were defeated.
sentences.zh: 在金赛尔战役中，爱尔兰和西班牙联军战败。

sentences.en: O’Neill submitted to the English Crown in 1603.
sentences.zh: O'Neill 于 1603 年向英国王室臣服。

sentences.en: And then, in 1607, something happened that closed a chapter of Irish history for good.
sentences.zh: 接着，在 1607 年，发生了一件彻底终结爱尔兰历史某一章节的事情。

sentences.en: One autumn morning, Hugh O’Neill and other leading Gaelic lords from Ulster, along with their families and followers, boarded ships and sailed away into self-imposed exile, to the more hospitable Catholic courts of Spain and Rome.
sentences.zh: 一个秋日的早晨，Hugh O'Neill 和其他来自阿尔斯特的主要盖尔领主，带着他们的家人和追随者登船离开，开始了自我流亡，前往对他们更友好的西班牙和罗马的天主教宫廷。

sentences.en: Whether they feared arrest or were seeking military support from abroad, historians still debate.
sentences.zh: 历史学家们至今仍在争论他们是因为害怕被捕，还是为了在国外寻求军事支持。

sentences.en: But they never came back. This event is called the Flight of the Earls.
sentences.zh: 但他们再也没有回来。这一事件被称为“伯爵外逃”（Flight of the Earls）。

sentences.en: It marked the end of Gaelic Ireland as a political force.
sentences.zh: 它标志着盖尔爱尔兰作为一个政治力量的终结。

sentences.en: The old aristocracy — the class that had maintained Gaelic culture and resisted English rule for centuries — it was gone.
sentences.zh: 旧贵族阶层——那个维持盖尔文化并反抗英国统治数个世纪的阶层——消失了。

sentences.en: And the land they left behind would not remain empty for long.
sentences.zh: 他们留下的土地并不会荒废太久。

sentences.en: The territories of the fled earls — six counties across the north of Ireland — were declared forfeit to the English Crown.
sentences.zh: 逃亡伯爵们的领地——爱尔兰北部的六个郡——被宣布收归英国王室所有。

sentences.en: And in 1610, the so-called Plantation of Ulster began.
sentences.zh: 1610 年，所谓的“阿尔斯特植民”（Plantation of Ulster）开始了。

sentences.en: Now, Ulster is the northernmost of Ireland's four provinces.
sentences.zh: 阿尔斯特是爱尔兰四个省份中最北端的一个。

sentences.en: It had been the most Gaelic, the most resistant to English rule.
sentences.zh: 它曾是最具盖尔特色、对英国统治反抗最激烈的地区。

sentences.en: Now it was to be transformed. The plan was for the land to be divided into parcels and distributed to settlers from England and Scotland.
sentences.zh: 现在它要被改造了。计划是将土地分成小块，分发给来自英格兰和苏格兰的定居者。

sentences.en: The Gaelic Catholic population who had lived on that land for centuries was pushed to the margins, where farming was harder.
sentences.zh: 在那片土地上生活了几个世纪的盖尔天主教人口被推向边缘地带，那里的耕作条件更加艰苦。

sentences.en: And by law, settlers were forbidden from renting land to native Irish tenants.
sentences.zh: 法律规定，禁止定居者将土地租给爱尔兰本地租户。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands of settlers came, particularly from the Lowlands of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 数以万计的定居者涌入，特别是来自苏格兰低地的人。

sentences.en: Now, Scotland and Ireland have a lot in common.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰和爱尔兰有很多共同点。

sentences.en: They are geographically close — you can almost see Scotland from the northern tip of Ireland on a clear day — but in the 17th century, Scotland and Ireland, culturally speaking, were very different places.
sentences.zh: 它们地理位置相近——在晴朗的日子里，你几乎可以从爱尔兰北端望见苏格兰——但在 17 世纪，从文化上讲，苏格兰和爱尔兰是截然不同的地方。

sentences.en: The Scots were Protestant. They spoke English.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰人是新教徒，他们说英语。

sentences.en: They had no connection to Ireland or its traditions.
sentences.zh: 他们与爱尔兰及其传统没有任何联系。

sentences.en: The two communities that emerged did not mix.
sentences.zh: 形成的这两个社群互不往来。

sentences.en: And of course, they were not supposed to mix.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们本就不该融合。

sentences.en: New towns were built on defensive plans.
sentences.zh: 新城镇是根据防御计划建造的。

sentences.en: The settlers and the displaced native Irish lived side by side, but they worshipped in different churches, spoke different languages, and saw both the land and its future in completely different ways: for the settlers, it had been lawfully granted by the Crown; for the native Irish, it had been taken from them.
sentences.zh: 定居者和流离失所的爱尔兰本地人并肩生活，但他们在不同的教堂礼拜，说不同的语言，对土地及其未来的看法也完全不同：对定居者来说，这是王室合法授予的；对本地爱尔兰人来说，这是从他们手中夺走的。

sentences.en: There is a direct, traceable line from the decision to colonise Ulster in 1610 to the partition of Ireland three hundred years later — the division of the island that you can still see on the map today.
sentences.zh: 从 1610 年殖民阿尔斯特的决定，到 300 年后爱尔兰的分治——也就是你今天在地图上仍能看到的岛屿划分——有着直接且可追溯的联系。

sentences.en: Now, we've already had a few "hate figures", in the form of Henry II and Henry VIII, people whose portraits you won't find on the wall in many Irish pubs.
sentences.zh: 我们已经提到了几个“仇恨人物”，比如 Henry II 和 Henry VIII，在许多爱尔兰酒吧的墙上你是找不到他们的画像的。

sentences.en: But they pale in comparison to who comes next, a man whose name is still spoken with bitterness in Ireland today: Oliver Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 但与接下来的这个人相比，他们就相形见绌了。在今天的爱尔兰，提起这个人的名字依然充满苦涩：Oliver Cromwell。

sentences.en: Now, before we get to what he did in Ireland, I need to give you some context on Oliver Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 在讲他在爱尔兰的所作所为之前，我需要给你们介绍一下 Oliver Cromwell 的背景。

sentences.en: In England in the 1640s, there had been a civil war between King Charles I and the Parliament — the body that governed alongside the king.
sentences.zh: 17 世纪 40 年代的英格兰，国王 Charles I 与议会（与国王共同治理国家的机构）之间爆发了内战。

sentences.en: Cromwell was the military leader of the winning Parliamentary side.
sentences.zh: Cromwell 是获胜的议会派的军事领袖。

sentences.en: And in 1649, after his victory, he did something that shocked Europe: he put the king on trial and had him executed.
sentences.zh: 1649 年，在取得胜利后，他做了一件震惊欧洲的事：他审判了国王并将其处决。

sentences.en: By the way, if you would like to hear more about that, episode 232 tells that story, of when Britain killed its king.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，如果你想了解更多，第 232 集讲述了英国处死国王的故事。

sentences.en: Anyway, after the execution of King Charles I, England became a republic, with Cromwell at its head.
sentences.zh: 总之，在 Charles I 被处决后，英格兰成为了共和国，由 Cromwell 领导。

sentences.en: He was a deeply religious Protestant, with an absolute conviction that he was doing God's work.
sentences.zh: 他是一个极其虔诚的新教徒，坚信自己是在履行上帝的旨意。

sentences.en: And he did not conceal his contempt for Irish Catholicism.
sentences.zh: 他从不掩饰对爱尔兰天主教的蔑视。

sentences.en: He believed the Catholic population of Ireland was a direct threat to England's new republic.
sentences.zh: 他认为爱尔兰的天主教人口对英格兰的新共和国构成了直接威胁。

sentences.en: And so in August 1649, he arrived in Ireland with an army of around twelve thousand men.
sentences.zh: 于是，1649 年 8 月，他率领约一万两千人的军队抵达爱尔兰。

sentences.en: He came to put down a Catholic alliance and to punish those responsible for violence against Protestant settlers eight years earlier.
sentences.zh: 他来是为了镇压天主教联盟，并惩罚那些在八年前对新教定居者实施暴力的人。

sentences.en: He was brutally efficient and utterly without mercy.
sentences.zh: 他手段残暴、效率极高，且绝不留情。

sentences.en: At Drogheda — a town north of Dublin — the Irish soldiers defending the town refused to surrender.
sentences.zh: 在都柏林北部的德罗赫达（Drogheda）镇，防守该镇的爱尔兰士兵拒绝投降。

sentences.en: What followed was a massacre. Several thousand people were killed: soldiers, civilians, and Catholic clergy sheltering inside the town.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一场大屠杀。数千人被杀：包括士兵、平民以及在镇内避难的天主教神职人员。

sentences.en: Cromwell described it in a letter home as God's righteous judgement.
sentences.zh: Cromwell 在家信中将其描述为上帝的正义审判。

sentences.en: The following month, a similar thing happened at Wexford.
sentences.zh: 次月，类似的事情在韦克斯福德（Wexford）再次发生。

sentences.en: Thousands more died.
sentences.zh: 又有数千人丧生。

sentences.en: Cromwell left Ireland in 1650, but the campaign continued for another three years under his officers.
sentences.zh: Cromwell 于 1650 年离开爱尔兰，但军事行动在他的军官领导下又持续了三年。

sentences.en: The human cost was devastating. Hundreds of thousands of people died — from battle, from the famines that followed the destruction of the countryside, and from disease.
sentences.zh: 伤亡人数是毁灭性的。数十万人死亡——死于战斗、死于破坏乡村后引发的饥荒，以及死于疾病。

sentences.en: A population of perhaps one and a half million in 1641 may have fallen to fewer than a million by 1652.
sentences.zh: 1641 年约 150 万的人口，到 1652 年可能已降至不足 100 万。

sentences.en: The land settlement that followed was as brutal as the military campaign.
sentences.zh: 随后的土地安置政策与军事行动一样残酷。

sentences.en: Catholic landowners lost their estates. Those who survived were ordered west of the River Shannon — to Connacht, the western province of Ireland, the most remote and poorest part of the island.
sentences.zh: 天主教地主失去了他们的庄园。幸存者被命令迁往香农河（River Shannon）以西——前往爱尔兰西部的康诺特（Connacht）省，那是岛上最偏远、最贫困的地方。

sentences.en: And there's a famous phrase that entered Irish historical memory from this period, "To Hell or to Connacht".
sentences.zh: 这一时期有一句名言进入了爱尔兰的历史记忆：“要么下地狱，要么去康诺特”。

sentences.en: Before 1641, Catholics had owned roughly sixty percent of the land in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 1641 年之前，天主教徒拥有爱尔兰约 60% 的土地。

sentences.en: By 1660, they owned an estimated twenty percent.
sentences.zh: 到 1660 年，他们拥有的土地估计仅剩 20%。

sentences.en: And the Cromwellian settlement created the social structure that would define Ireland for the next two centuries.
sentences.zh: 克伦威尔式的安置政策创造了定义爱尔兰未来两个世纪的社会结构。

sentences.en: A Protestant landowning class sat at the top.
sentences.zh: 一个新教地主阶级处于顶层。

sentences.en: A Catholic majority of tenants and workers lived beneath them, on land that had once been their own, or their parents', or their grandparents'.
sentences.zh: 占人口多数的天主教租户和工人生活在他们之下，生活在曾经属于他们自己、或他们父母、祖父母的土地上。

sentences.en: Everyone knew it. The awareness of that dispossession ran like a fault line through everything that followed.
sentences.zh: 每个人都心知肚明。这种被剥夺感像一条断层线，贯穿了随后发生的一切。

sentences.en: Almost five centuries earlier, the exiled King Diarmait had invited the English over to Ireland.
sentences.zh: 大约五个世纪前，流亡国王 Diarmait 邀请英国人来到爱尔兰。

sentences.en: It would prove to be a decision that would forever change the country, and one that the people of Ireland would spend the next 800 years trying to undo.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这是一个永远改变这个国家的决定，也是爱尔兰人民在接下来的 800 年里试图撤销的决定。

sentences.en: The story of what comes next — the Act of Union, the Great Famine, the Civil War, and the road to the Republic — that is what we have coming up in parts two and three.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的故事——《联合法案》、大饥荒、内战以及通往共和国之路——就是我们将在第二和第三部分中讲述的内容。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode — the first part of our three-part series on Ireland's long road to independence.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的节目就到这里——这是我们关于爱尔兰漫长独立之路三集系列节目的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up we'll be moving into the nineteenth century: the Act of Union that bound Ireland formally to Britain, the Great Famine, and the early movements for self-determination.
sentences.zh: 下一集我们将进入 19 世纪：将爱尔兰正式与英国绑在一起的《联合法案》、大饥荒，以及早期的民族自决运动。

sentences.en: And in part three, it's rebellion, revolution, and the path to independence.
sentences.zh: 在第三部分，将是反抗、革命和通往独立之路。

sentences.en: We also have a bonus member-only episode on The Troubles, which is episode number 507, so you can really do a binge listen on Irish history, as well as pretty much anything else.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一集关于“北爱尔兰问题”（The Troubles）的会员专享加更节目，即第 507 集，所以你可以一口气听完爱尔兰历史，以及几乎任何其他内容。

sentences.en: You can find out more about that over at leonardoenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 leonardoenglish.com 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝大家平安，我们下期节目再见。
